title: 6.3.2 Sub-build: Slow to a stop
description: One ball, moving, and a rule that calls it stopped. No table, no pockets.

steps.title: Run it
steps.instructions: The ball slides for ever at the same speed: nothing slows it.

steps.title: Add drag
steps.instructions: In `setup()`, set `cue.drag = 0.02;`. Run it: the ball slows, but never stops exactly.

steps.title: Call it stopped
steps.instructions: In `draw()`, when `cue.speed < 0.2`, set `cue.speed = 0`. Now the ball really stops.
hints: The threshold is a small number, not zero.
Show the speed with text so you can watch it fall.

requirements.title: Drag is set
requirements.description: The ball has a drag above 0. Help: 6.3.1 (Reading: Rolling to a stop)

requirements.title: Stopped is a threshold
requirements.description: The speed is tested against a small number and set to 0 (or a flag). Help: 6.3.1 (Reading: Rolling to a stop)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch for "Sub-build: Slow to a stop". The task: give the ball drag and call it stopped when its speed falls under a small number, setting the speed to 0. Accept any names, helpers, ternaries and semicolons; a line only in a comment or string does not count. Short, plain notes for a 14-year-old; never write corrected code.

rubric.title: A threshold, not zero
rubric.description: The stop test compares speed with a small number, then sets it to 0 or sets a flag.

rubric.title: It can be seen
rubric.description: The speed or a stopped/rolling word is shown, so the change is visible.
